novelty_flags.label: novelty_justification and seed dynamic-face-pasting
novelty_flags.one_line: The proposal attributes the static weak-shadow sharpness/full-rank result to Chen et al. “Theorem 1,” but the inspected cited arXiv version places that claim in Section 3.1, Theorem 3.2; correct the anchor throughout.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 3 (Chen reduction)
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed reduction does not define the “observed-cell shadow matrix,” nor does its stated positivity condition index the baseline-state/action cells required to identify the precise Chen matrix and cellwise static program.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states sharp identification for its static weak-shadow mean problem and says point identification obtains when A_x has full column rank; the result is numbered Theorem 3.2, not Theorem 1.

source_verification_receipts.version: Mathematics of Operations Research 30(2), 2005 version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves robust finite- and infinite-horizon dynamic-programming counterparts when the set of conditional measures has a rectangularity property.
Discrete causal questions are reduced to polynomial programming and the algorithm continually refines certified non-sharp ranges with an epsilon-sharpness guarantee.
The paper studies monotone missingness in OPE, proposes an inverse-probability-weighted estimator for nonignorable missingness, and performs inference.

The paper uses future states as shadows, assumes the exclusion S_{t+1} ⟂ O_t conditional on current reward/state/action, invokes completeness, and allows target policies to depend on previous missingness indicators.

The paper constructs Monte-Carlo criterion-level confidence sets for identified sets and subvectors, with coverage results for regular, cone, singular, point-identified, and partially identified models.
Under its shadow-variable setup, the paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient condition for identification of a static mean functional without identifying the full data law.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Rewrite the H=1 reduction with an explicit map from each (S_1,A_1)-conditioned observed table to Chen et al.'s A_x and beta_x, state the required cell positivity and rank condition, and replace every incorrect “Theorem 1” anchor with Theorem 3.2.

Promote the strictness OEQ into a field-grade theorem target by fixing a smallest binary-action/three-reward two-stage family and stating the actual observable minors whose signs certify a nonempty relatively open strictness region.

Give the exact finite polynomial encoding of the multinomial likelihood-ratio fiber, including the finite quantile-order partition, so the claimed certified optimizer is explicitly applicable rather than merely described as semialgebraic.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Chen sanity-reduction specification and citation anchor, then retain the dynamic strict-containment OEQ as the field-tier novelty kernel.
